choreo.doc: M2-BPR-01/02: battle choreography (docs/kb/tech/battle_presentation.md). BattleChoreo plays each resolved action as beats: approach (the actor travels), strike (the action's clip, or its procedural motion), contact (at strike start + contact_at x strike_sec: the target reacts, damage floats and hit VFX land), recover, return. A KO collapses ko.delay_sec after contact. All times are seconds at battle speed 1.0; distances are metres. travel: 'target' runs to stop_short_m in front of the target(s); 'step' steps step_m toward them; 'none' stays on the mark. lunge_m, lift_m, crouch_m and lean_deg shape the procedural strike on a stand-in with no clip.

dive.doc: M2-BPR-04 Lamp Dive (Rhen): a leap that rises arc_m over the approach, then a plunge onto the target; contact on the plunge.

verse.doc: M2-BPR-04 Shallows Verse (Asha): a chant held long; every healed ally lifts in turn, stagger_sec apart.

brace.doc: M2-BPR-04 Return Tide (Toma): planted, he takes the tide (windup_m back and down at windup_at), then answers it with one counter thrust.

glyph.doc: M2-BPR-04 Written Light (Ysolde): a glyph written in the air, trace_strokes strokes side to side, finished on the contact; the light reaches each foe in turn.

swing.doc: M3-BPR-422 the weighted swing (Kerrid's Swell; kerrid.md finisher clip): he closes in, swings the cleaver back and holds it coiled (windup_m back and down at windup_at, through the long strike), then hauls it through flat and low; contact late on the release.

reel.doc: M3-BPR-422 the reel-stop (Liss's Swell; her finisher clip): she steps out and winds the reel at the hip (windup_m back), then throws the gloved hand down and forward and the gadget goes off on the foe; each foe it reaches flinches stagger_sec after the last.

toll.doc: M2-BPR-04 the Drownbell's Toll: the bell rears back (windup_m) and lurches down on the toll; every party member recoils hard (react_scale) as the shockwave reaches it (wave_m_s: BattleBossVfx's ring, boss_vfx.json toll (ring_radius_m - 0.2) / ring_s).

style_by_actor.doc: M3-BPR-408: a style by the actor's enemy id and the skill's kind, after style_by_skill (a signature move whose skill ids are not written yet). The Avalanche Ram's own low 'charge' style waits on its sound row (request M3-BPR-410 to audio); until then it plays the melee. The Wakefin (10-30) strikes from the water beside the barge, so its blows stay in place and never run onto the deck.

swell_style_by_hero.doc: M3-BPR-422: the style a hero's Swell technique plays when style_by_skill has no row for it (Kerrid's weighted swing and Liss's reel-stop, whose technique ids combat has not written yet: M3-C05-06, M3-C06-05). By hero id.

reaction.doc: The target's reaction on the contact beat. damage: recoil_m away from the actor and tilt_deg back, out and back over sec; heal: a lift_m rise; miss: a sidestep of dodge_m; push (M3-BPR-411): a hit that only pushes its target down the timeline (the ward shoved back by Rope Dive, Grip the Stair, Hand Closes; Drag Net) staggers it recoil_m back; immune (M3-BPR-406): a blow on a damage-immune foe (the Reach's Breach) stops dead, a stiff sideways shudder of shudder_m, shudders times over sec, no recoil, none under reduced motion. clip names the model clip tried first (the clip contract).

phase_looks.doc: M3-BPR-406 BattlePhaseLooks: a foe whose phase makes it untargetable (the Reach's Breach) fades every surface to untargetable.alpha until the phase ends, so the player sees why their aim is refused (Pillar 4).

telegraph.doc: M3-BPR-413 BattleTelegraph: a foe gathering a charged skill (a skill row's charge) draws itself in and sways on that action's contact and on each later turn of the charge, so the stage agrees with the timeline's intent (Pillar 4). A boss whose bosses row gathers that charge keeps its own.

counter.doc: M3-BPR-406 (ADR 0100): a counter stance answers a landed physical hit at once: the hero's attack clip starts delay_sec after the blow's strike ends, and the attacker's reaction lands on that clip's contact frame (clip only: the attacker keeps its run). Felled by it, the attacker collapses once it is home.

withdraw.doc: M3-BPR-406 (ADR 0100): a withdrawn foe is not felled: it backs away from the party by back_m over sec (eased in, at the battle speed) and is hidden; reduced motion hides it in place.

spacing.doc: M3-BPR-402: a melee run stops so the actor, at the end of its lunge, keeps its radius + each body's radius + clearance_m from everyone in its path: heroes and creatures never interpenetrate. A radius is the model's footprint (the mean of its meshes' half-width and half-depth about the stand-in's origin, times footprint_k), else battle_sandbox.json stand_ins radius for a primitive.
spacing.lineup_doc: M3-BPR-403 BattleLineup: at spawn each side is pushed apart on the ground until every pair keeps both footprints + clearance_m, each fighter at most lineup_max_shift_m off its mark (lineup_iters passes).
spacing.tall_to_back_doc: The encounter sweep (10-30): the opening foes are seated tallest farthest from the camera (stand-in height plus hover), so a tall foe never hides a short one at rest (the Lantern Eel over the Gull Harrier on the causeway). BattleStage._seat_order.
spacing.detour_doc: M3-BPR-402: a melee run that a body beside its path stops short turns by detour_step_deg each way, up to detour_max_deg, taking the smallest turn that ends within detour_reach_m of where an unobstructed run would (it comes at the target from a little to one side).

impact.doc: M3-BPR-401 BattleImpact, the battle feel on the contact beat. A hit's strength (0..1) is its damage over the target's max HP, 1 at full_frac; a crit adds crit_bonus. Hit-stop: from heavy_strength, the choreography clock and the actor's and targets' clips hold for hit_stop_frames [lo, hi] (lerped by strength) at stop_fps. Shake: from shake_min_strength, BattleStage.shake at shake_scale [lo, hi]. Flash: a warm light pulse at the hardest-hit target, energy [lo, hi] capped at energy_cap, range_m, at height_frac of its height, back to dark over sec. recoil_scale [lo, hi] scales each damage reaction (and reaction.damage.clip_recoil_k a model with its own hit clip). ko_slowmo: the blow that fells the last foe slows the clock to factor for sec from lead_sec before the collapse. reduced_motion: shake_scale (0 = none), flash_scale, slowmo_factor.

enter.doc: A fighter swapped or called in walks onto its mark from back_m behind it.

choreo.accent_doc: M2-BPR-04 accents (BattleChoreo.accent): a short overlay on a fighter's root, out and back over sec. lift_m/crouch_m up/down; recoil_m and tilt_deg back, away from the other side (negative leans in); sway_deg side to side, sways times; clip (optional) a contract clip.

bosses.doc: M2-BPR-04 BattleBossChoreo, by enemy row id. charge_skill: the charge whose gather sways the boss (on the gathering action's contact, then each turn of the charge); break: the boss's stagger on the rim-breaking blow's contact; flood: on phase_changed to phase, the party braces in slot order (stagger_sec apart) once the action playing is done. The toll's own motion is the 'toll' style.

opened.doc: M3-BPR-408: the Lamp Engine opens (Ch11): its core rises a little as the housing parts (never gold mote-light); the party steadies in turn.

uprooted.doc: M3-BPR-418: the Mangrove Drowner tears free of its tree (Ch10, act2_roster.md) and stands up on its roots like legs: its root lifts and rocks as the creature's own phase_change clip plays; the party braces in turn. A quiet fear, no glow added here (the motes that go upward are VFX).

wakefin.doc: M3-BPR-418: the Wakefin fights in the dark (Ch15, act2_roster.md): its telegraphs are sound and sea-glow, never light. On stage, any charge it gathers sinks its blade under the water and holds it there, slowly (no flash, no glow added); the camera closes in a step a turn (camera.pressure.by_enemy). The timeline shows its intent as for any foe.

vowbound.doc: M2-BPR-04 BattleVowboundChoreo. call: the caller's accent as it calls; step_off: the party walks back off the field in slot order (delay_sec + stagger_sec x slot); entry: the Vowbound rises depth_m out of the water at its slot after delay_sec, tipped lean_deg forward and straightening (longer than a swap's walk-in); dismiss: it sinks back (after the action playing, a battle won included); fall: struck down, it takes the blow, then tips back tilt_deg and is drawn under, slower; return: the party walks back in (choreo enter) once share of the exit has played, stagger_sec apart. clip_own (M3-CRE-639): the clip the Vowbound's own model plays instead of clip when it has it (Ilun's rise and dismiss).

reduced_motion.doc: UiSettings reduced motion: shorter travel and leans, no tilt on reactions.

speeds.doc: UiSettings battle_speed values (accessibility.json) the sequencer accepts.

outro.doc: M2-BPR-05: after the last action's choreography. victory: the standing party plays the victory clip, or a stand-in hops `hops` times hop_m high over sec, each fighter stagger_sec after the last, after delay_sec. escape: the party walks back_m back off the field over sec. The result panel waits for it plus settle_sec.

camera.doc: M2-BPR-03: the battle camera director (docs/kb/tech/battle_presentation.md, Camera director). Every shot is framed off the battle axis (party to foes, from the camera's authored default) so the party stays screen-right and the foes screen-left: the line is never crossed and the camera never rolls. anchor 'actor' is the actor's mark, 'strike' its strike point, 'target' the targets' middle, 'default' the authored default. A placed shot sits back_m behind the anchor along the axis, side_m toward the default camera's side and up_m above it, and looks at the point look_at of the way from the actor's mark to the targets, raised look_up_m. A 'default' shot moves push of the way from the default toward the raised targets and turns look_at of the way to them. fov (degrees) is optional: none keeps the default's. Blends: in over blend_in_sec from the sequence start, to the contact shot over to_contact_sec ending on the contact, out over blend_out_sec ending exactly on the sequence end (held at least hold_contact_sec after the contact). A shot that would put a target outside safe_frame (fractions of the screen kept clear for the HUD, at the design aspect) or the actor's head at its strike point off screen falls back to the default. by_style: a party action's lead and contact shots per style ('' holds the lead); enemy: every enemy action.
camera.water_clear_doc: A camera moment's lens stays this far above a boss's flood water (BattleBossVfx.water_y): the Drownbell's phase moment sat at the risen waterline, the water edge-on and invisible.

bystanders.doc: The encounter sweep (10-29): a contact shot whose sight line to a target's middle crosses a fighter that is neither the actor nor a target (an ally on its mark, another foe) keeps the default frame. Each bystander's bounds are shrunk about their middle by shrink first, so a held spear or a hem does not veto the shot.

pressure.doc: M3-BPR-406: while a foe gathers one of these telegraphed skills the resting frame narrows by up to max_fov_deg, a step each turn its charge counts down (turns: the charge's length). None under reduced motion.

enemy_by_skill.doc: M3-BPR-420 (ADR 0041): the Act I bosses' big moves get a shot, not the enemy's default push. A heavy single blow frames the boss at its strike point, then the hero it hits (boss_blow, target); a move on the whole party frames the boss winding up from its mark (boss_sweep) and then holds wide. Checked before enemy_by_actor; a shot that fails the safe frame falls back to the default. A foe whose body at its strike point stands across the lens's sight of its targets drops that shot (the director's body check). The Reach keeps the default frame for all its moves: at its size every placed shot saw only its body or dropped under the wall-head, while the default frame already shows its hand over the party.

moments.doc: M3-BPR-426 (BattleBossCamera): a boss fight's camera moments besides its intro and its big moves. phase: once the action that changed the boss's phase has played, the camera eases over in_sec to the boss as its intro frames it (the hero shot), holds hold_sec, and eases home over out_sec; fall: the same on the boss as it falls to the finishing blow. The boss is the encounter's boss_intro row's enemy. None under reduced motion or skipped animations; the next turn waits for it.

entry.doc: M3-BPR-1325 (BattleEntryCamera): a set piece's entry acting (the Climb) eases to the arena's camera hint for its role (hints: role -> node path under the arena; env-art-b's seawall arenas carry CameraHints/the_stair_head, looking over the stair head, and CameraHints/along_the_walk, down the wall-walk), looking look_m ahead, at fov.
entry.skills_doc: M3-BPR-406: skills limits a role's cut to those skills; once cuts that role's first such turn only. The Kirru (wave 3's guest) cuts along the wall-walk (the movers in front, the party behind them) the first time Pell sounds Storm-Call; the withdrawal it brings plays on the home frame, where the player sees which spawn leaves.

rest_by_enemy.doc: M3-BPR-425 (the PC's GPU QA row 36: the Reach's arm filled most of the frame and passed over the party all fight): a foe too big for the authored frame moves its fight's rest frame back_m along the view and up_m higher, still on the authored look point, at fov. The Reach: 40% of the screen and the party outside the safe frame at the authored rest; with creatures-b's boss_seats (M3-CRB-011: the Reach, the Matron and the Spar-Wraith sit on their own marks) these rows finish the frame: the Reach 4 m back and 2 m up (its hand grips the wall beside the party, the party and the sea read), the Spar-Wraith 3 m back and 1.5 m up (its masts were out of the top of the frame). The Matron's seat needs no row. Each viewed in its own arena.

enemy_by_actor.doc: M3-BPR-408: a foe whose actions get their own framing, by its enemy id (otherwise enemy). The Avalanche Ram's charge rides side-on (the boss camera sheet, 10-30: from 0.25 m up and 5.2 m out, Toma's shield stood across the Ram and its head left the frame; 1.0 m up and 7.2 m out keep both).

summon_cinematic.doc: M2-BPR-08 C10, BattleSummonCinematic: a Vowbound's first call in a live story battle (first_call_flags: its seen-flag, declared in flags.tres) under UiSettings summon_cinematic (the UI track's row): 'short' (default) = the first call only, 'full' = every call, 'off' = off_entry (no rise). entry replaces vowbound.entry: the water stills for delay_sec after the party steps off, then the Vowbound rises depth_m over sec, tipped lean_deg; hold_sec more after it stands. Bound light (color script C10: glimmer_bound, steady): an OmniLight3D light_height_m above its slot, light_energy reached over light_in_sec from light_at_sec, light_range_m. Camera: the 'summon' shot (camera.shots), in over camera_in_sec, back to the default over the last camera_out_sec.

placeholder_clips.doc: M2-BPR-10, BattlePlaceholderClips: until the heroes' battle clips land (M2-CHR-07), a model with a Skeleton3D and an AnimationPlayer gets a generated pose clip for every contract clip it lacks; a real clip of that name always wins. bones: role -> candidate bone names, the first the skeleton has wins (the MPFB2 rig as the characters track exports it, DEF-*, then MPFB2's default names). A skeleton that resolves fewer than min_roles roles (a creature) gets nothing. A pose is role -> [x, y, z] degrees, a turn in the model's axes (X = the fighter's left, Y = up, Z = the way it faces; composed YXZ) on top of what the bone inherits, as the characters' hero_clips.py writes them: +X bends the spine forward and swings a hanging limb backward, +Y turns to the fighter's left, +Z tilts to its right. base is the standing pose (arms down from the rest); a key's pose replaces base per role, a key with no pose is base, and hips_m moves the hips role (metres, model axes). Every clip keys every role named in base or any clip, so no limb is left in the last clip's pose. A strike clip's blow key sits at its main style's contact_at x strike_sec.
placeholder_clips.max_key_deg_doc: M2-HER-1114: the widest turn between two consecutive rotation keys of one bone; a wider pair gets slerped keys between, each key on the previous key's hemisphere (a near-antipodal pair flipped Ysolde's arm mid cross-fade).

boss_intro.doc: M3-BPR-02 BattleBossIntro (docs/kb/tech/battle_presentation.md, Boss intros): at a boss encounter's first turn, once the screen is uncovered and any opening banner is done (at most reveal_wait_max_sec), the camera eases from the default to the row's shot (camera.shots, framed on the row's enemy; a shot that fails the safe frame keeps the default) over camera_in_sec, holds hold_sec, and eases home over camera_out_sec. The title card (title_key over epithet_key, the UI theme) fades in over card_in_sec from card_at_sec and out over card_out_sec, ending as the camera turns home; it rises rise_px as it fades in (none under reduced motion, which also keeps the camera on the default). card: its CanvasLayer layer, its rect at the 1920x1080 reference (clear of the timeline), the label variations, the title's height, the gold rule under the name (rule_y, rule_length, rule_px) and the dark band behind it (band_alpha, band_fade). The first turn waits for it (BattleHud.holds_battle). Confirm or cancel skips it. on_retry: whether Fight again plays it again (default false). Instant pacing and skip animations play none.

hero.doc: M3-BPR-423 (the Lead, 03:41): the boss intro's hero shot (BattleBossHeroShot), tried before the row's fitted shot. A low lens (cam_height_m above the boss's ground) on the viewer's side looks up at the boss from yaw_deg off the boss-to-party line, at each fov in turn (a longer lens from farther keeps the party out of a tall boss's frame), at the distance (min_m..max_m, plus half the boss's breadth) where the boss's height fills `fill` of the screen; it aims at look_frac of the boss's height. The boss's top stays inside the safe frame, its middle inside the safe sides, its upper body (head_frac of its height) clear of the title card (the feet may pass behind it); no arena mesh stands between the lens and the boss; no party member crowds the frame (party_max_h of the screen tall at most, clear of the timeline: big14's formation stands Toma on the viewer's side, so the party is often in a hero shot, which is welcome). Biggest fill first; a pose with a party member in frame is preferred. A row's hero false keeps the fitted shot.

fit.doc: M3-BPR-404: the shot keeps its angle and fov but its distance fits the boss model's bounds (a sphere around its visible meshes) in the narrower field of view at margin; look_drop (of the radius) aims below the centre so the boss sits above the card; min_m and max_m clamp the distance; until the boss's top and bottom are inside the safe frame and its feet clear the title card's top edge by card_clear_px (1080 reference), it first aims lower (look_drop + drop_step steps up to drop_max) and then widens (x widen_step on the clamped distance, up to widen_max); the closest pose that holds wins (none clearing the card: the closest that passes the safe frame). A row's fit_margin overrides margin; fit false keeps the shot's own offsets.
fit.party_doc: M3-BPR-404 (big11 playtest: Toma huge over the timeline): every party member is off screen, or inside the safe frame at most party_max_h of the screen tall; the search orbits the shot about the boss by yaw_steps_deg (its own angle first) to find such a frame. 0.36, not 0.3 (PC render c1d1e3e): Hullgnaw's approved frame has Rhen 0.35 tall at its side; 0.3 widened it past the raft's rail.

boss_intro.by_enemy_doc: M3-BPR-408: intro rows by the boss's enemy id, for bosses whose encounters are not written yet (Act II). An encounter's own row (rows) wins; otherwise the first foe with a by_enemy row gets it. Same keys as rows, without enemy.
